method: Pearson correlation, one value per year, between modelled water stress and the standardised anomaly (z-score, sample standard deviation) of growing-season MODIS NDVI at the field-centre pixel. Modelled stress is 1 − ΣETa/ΣETc of rain-fed winter wheat (sown 15 November, harvested 12 July) from 1 April to harvest, from the engine's daily FAO-56 chapter 8 root-zone water balance on NASA POWER precipitation and Penman-Monteith ET0 with the field's SoilGrids available water capacity. The same comparison is made for a baseline climatic dryness index, 1 − ΣP/ΣET0 over April–September. 95 % intervals are paired percentile bootstraps over years (10,000 resamples, seed 2026). Protocol fixed in advance in docs/VALIDATION.md.
caveats: Model (winter-wheat water balance): r = -0.66, 95 % interval -0.85 to -0.43. Baseline (April–September 1 − P/ET0): r = -0.53, 95 % interval -0.74 to -0.26. Difference model − baseline: -0.13, 95 % interval -0.34 to +0.03. No detectable difference between the model and the baseline: the interval of the difference includes 0.
The land use of the pixel is not known. The model assumes rain-fed winter wheat; if the pixel holds an irrigated or summer crop, orchard, pasture or a mix, its greenness follows other drivers.
Irrigation is not represented: irrigated fields can stay green in dry years, which weakens the relationship.
NDVI is a single 250 m pixel; it may mix several fields and land uses.
24 years is a small sample; the correlation is uncertain and shows association, not causation.

provenance.dataset: NASA POWER daily point data, Agroclimatology community (API v2.10.3)
provenance.provider: NASA Langley Research Center, POWER Project
provenance.note: Gridded, model-based reanalysis values for the grid cell containing the field, not field measurements: MERRA-2 meteorology (0.5° × 0.625°) and CERES SYN1deg solar radiation (1° × 1°). Parameters T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2MDEW, WS2M, PS, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, PRECTOTCORR, GWETROOT. Daily reference evapotranspiration is FAO-56 Penman-Monteith (eq. 6) with actual vapour pressure from the dew point (eq. 14) and net radiation from eqs. 37–40 using the POWER grid-cell elevation (676 m); annual ET0 is the sum of daily values. Hargreaves (eq. 52) was used on 0 day(s) where Penman-Monteith inputs were missing. Root-zone wetness is the GWETROOT fraction of saturation from the MERRA-2 land model, not a measured soil moisture.

provenance.dataset: SoilGrids 2.0 (clay, sand, silt, soc, phh2o; mean and 5th/95th percentiles)
provenance.temporal_coverage: Static; predictions from soil profiles collected over several decades
provenance.note: Texture class (USDA), organic carbon and pH are depth-weighted means of 0–30 cm. Available water capacity is the 0–100 cm sum of field capacity (−33 kPa) minus wilting point (−1500 kPa) from the Saxton & Rawls (2006) pedotransfer functions (Soil Sci. Soc. Am. J. 70:1569–1578), with organic matter = 1.724 × organic carbon; gravel and salinity are not accounted for. SoilGrids 90 % prediction interval for 0–30 cm at this point: clay 3–92 %, organic carbon 2.9–44.2 g/kg; values derived from the mean prediction carry that uncertainty.

provenance.dataset: MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250 m (MOD13Q1 v061), NDVI and pixel reliability
provenance.provider: NASA LP DAAC (Didan 2021, doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061), served by the ORNL DAAC MODIS web service
provenance.note: Single 250 m pixel containing the field centre; it may include neighbouring fields, roads or buildings. Growing-season value = mean NDVI of the 10 composites starting day-of-year 97 to 241 (early April to late September) whose pixel reliability is 0 (good) or 1 (marginal); snow, cloud and fill are dropped and a year needs at least 6 usable composites. Fixture provenance: per-year values and intervals copied from docs/VALIDATION.md §3 (engine run of 14 November 2026); method, caveats and verdict wording generated by the engine's own code, because the ORNL MODIS service returned HTTP 503 when this fixture was built.

provenance.dataset: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 — Crop evapotranspiration
provenance.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
provenance.note: Crop coefficients (Table 12, adjusted for local wind and humidity with eqs. 62 and 65), stage lengths (Table 11), rooting depth and depletion fraction (Table 22), daily root-zone water balance and water-stress coefficient Ks (chapter 8, eqs. 84–85) and bare-soil evaporation between crops (chapter 7, eqs. 73–74, Table 19). Runoff and capillary rise are not modelled.
